mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during periods of sustained sub-3.5% unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes purchasing power, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate revenues and profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which initially boosts consumer spending but eventually raises wage growth and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in an otherwise neutral macro environment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes under neutral policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rebound in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months after a prior six-month contraction signals a supply-chain recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and capital spending, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months after 6-month contraction
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 40% of triggered post-contraction episodes.
